question: In July 2, 1959 United States standards for grades of processed fruits, vegetables, and certain other products listed as dehydrated, consider the items in the "dried and dehydrated section" specifically marked as dehydrated along with any items in the Frozen/Chilled section that contain the whole name of the item, but not if they're marked Chilled. As of August 2023, what is the percentage (to the nearest percent) of those standards that have been superseded by a new version since the date given in the 1959 standards?

mistake_reason: At step 5, the orchestrator accepted a visibly truncated and partially obscured list from the BHL scan and instructed the team to proceed without requesting clarification or retrieval of the complete, precise list. The orchestrator did not ask WebSurfer to verify that each item was explicitly marked “dehydrated” (it allowed inclusion of items labeled only as “dried,” like prunes and figs) nor clarify the exact matching rule for Frozen/Chilled items. This failure to ask for clarification led to using an incomplete and ambiguous dataset as definitive, causing an incorrect denominator and inclusion of non-qualifying items, ultimately producing the wrong supersession percentage.
